Magnetic [microrobotics](../index.qmd) refers to the field of research and development focused on creating and controlling tiny robotic devices that can navigate and perform tasks using magnetic fields [@nelson2008micro; @abbott2020magnetic]. 
These robots generally have a size of less than a millimeter or of the order of a micrometer.

Magnetic microrobots are designed to take advantage of magnetic forces for their propulsion, manipulation, and control. 
They are often composed of [magnetic materials](magnetic-properties.qmd) or contain embedded magnetic elements such as nanoparticles or magnetic thin films.
By manipulating the external magnetic fields, one can guide and control the motion of these microrobots in various environments, including fluids, tissues, or confined spaces [@yang2021motion].

The magnetic fields used to control these microrobots can be generated by external electromagnets or by integrating miniaturized magnetic field sources on the microrobots themselves. 
The control techniques involve precise manipulation of the magnetic field gradients to induce forces and torques on the microrobots, enabling their movement and [manipulation](index.qmd).

Applications of magnetic microrobotics span across various fields, including biomedical applications, microsurgery, targeted drug delivery, microassembly, and microscale sensing. 
For example, magnetic microrobots can be used for targeted delivery of drugs to specific locations in the body, performing minimally invasive surgeries, or manipulating microscale objects in industrial settings.

The field of magnetic microrobotics is still an active area of research, with ongoing efforts to develop more advanced and versatile microrobots, improve their maneuverability, and enhance their capabilities for specific applications [@nelson2010microrobots; @yang2018grand].
